[size=5][b]What This Mod Does[/b][/size]


This mod reduces CPU usage by throttling background NPC updates. In vanilla Stardew Valley, every NPC updates 60 times per second, even when they're in a different location from the player. With large expansion mods like Stardew Valley Expanded, Ridgeside Village, or East Scarp adding 100+ NPCs, this constant updating can cause performance issues.


Background Tick Throttler selectively reduces how often NPCs in other locations update, while ensuring NPCs in your current location always update every frame to maintain smooth visual gameplay.



[size=5][b]How It Works[/b][/size]


The mod uses Harmony to patch the NPC update method. It implements a staggered throttling system:


[b]Always Updated (Every Frame):[/b]


[list]
[*]NPCs in your current location
[*]All monsters (combat functionality preserved)
[*]Your horse (smooth riding)
[*]Farm animals (egg/milk production unaffected)
[*]Pets
[*]Junimos (Community Center functionality)
[*]NPCs during cutscenes/events/festivals
[*]NPCs in active dialogue
[/list]


[b]Throttled (Reduced Updates):[/b]


[list]
[*]NPCs in other locations you're not currently visiting
[*]Update frequency controlled by the "Update Interval" setting
[/list]


The throttling uses a distributed algorithm (tick count + NPC ID modulo interval) to ensure NPCs don't all update on the same frame, providing smooth load distribution.

[/color][/b][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/41920/41920-1770001154-2119709508.png[/img]

[size=5][b]Configuration[/b][/size]


Configurable via Generic Mod Config Menu or by editing [font=Courier New]config.json[/font]:


[size=4][b]Enable Throttling (default: true)[/b][/size]


Turns the mod on/off.


[size=4][b]Update Interval (default: 2, range: 1-10)[/b][/size]


How often background NPCs update. Lower = smoother NPC behavior, higher = more CPU savings.


[list]
[*][b]1[/b] = No throttling (vanilla behavior)
[*][b]2[/b] = Update every other frame (recommended, safe balance)
[*][b]3-4[/b] = Moderate throttling (still safe for most scenarios)
[*][b]5-7[/b] = Noticeable background NPC behavior delays
[*][b]8-10[/b] = Very aggressive (may cause quest timing issues)
[/list]


[size=4][b]Always Update Villagers (default: false)[/b][/size]


If enabled, only throttles monsters/horses/junimos, never named villagers. This reduces CPU savings significantly but ensures villager schedules remain completely accurate.


[size=4][b]Enable Debug Logging (default: false)[/b][/size]


Shows performance statistics in SMAPI console every second. Useful for verifying the mod is working and measuring effectiveness.


[color=#ffff00][size=5][b]Known Limitations[/b][/size]
[/color]

[size=4][b]Schedule Delays[/b][/size]


NPCs in background locations will take longer in real time to complete their movement paths. For example, with Interval 2, an NPC moving between locations might take slightly longer in wall-clock time, but they'll still arrive at their scheduled destination at the correct in-game time because Stardew's schedule system is tick-based, not frame-based.


[size=4][b]Not Effective For[/b][/size]


[list]
[*]Initial game load times (all NPCs still need to load initially)
[*]Memory usage (NPCs remain in memory, just update less frequently)
[*]Graphics/rendering lag (this only affects NPC update logic)
[/list]


[size=4][b]Potential Issues[/b][/size]


[list]
[*]Timed quests with strict NPC meetup requirements [i]might[/i] be affected at high intervals (5+)
[*]Some modded events might not properly set event flags (protected in vanilla events)
[*]Multiplayer compatibility is untested
[/list]


[color=#00ff00][size=5][b]Safety Features - [/b][/size]
[/color]

[size=3]The mod includes extensive safety checks to prevent gameplay issues:
[/size]

[b]Combat Protection:[/b] All monsters always update every frame to ensure combat remains responsive and fair


[b]Farming Protection:[/b] Farm animals always update to ensure production mechanics work correctly


[b]Transportation Protection:[/b] Horses and pets always update for smooth player experience


[b]Event Protection:[/b] During cutscenes, festivals, and events, all NPCs update normally to prevent soft-locks


[b]Location Protection:[/b] NPCs in your current location never throttle to prevent visual stuttering


[b]Community Center Protection:[/b] Junimos always update to ensure bundle functionality


[b]Dialogue Protection:[/b] NPCs in active conversation always update


These protections ensure the game remains fully playable without broken mechanics, though they do reduce the theoretical maximum CPU savings.


[size=5][b]Compatibility[/b][/size]


[b]Compatible With:[/b]


[list]
[*]Stardew Valley Expanded
[*]Ridgeside Village
[*]East Scarp
[*]All NPC-adding mods
[*]Other performance mods (should stack)
[*]Content Patcher mods
[/list]


[b]Potential Conflicts:[/b]


[list]
[*]Other mods that patch [font=Courier New]NPC.update()[/font] (rare)
[*]Untested in multiplayer environments
[/list]

Enable debug logging in the config to see real-time statistics:

[/spoiler]


This helps verify the mod is working and shows exactly how many NPC update calls are being saved. Note that the percentage shown is of [i]NPC update calls[/i], not total game CPU usage.


[size=5][b]Installation[/b][/size]


[list]
[*]Install SMAPI (required)
[*]Install Generic Mod Config Menu (optional but recommended)
[*]Extract mod folder to [font=Courier New]Stardew Valley/Mods/[/font]
[*]Run game through SMAPI
[/list]

[size=4][b]For Maximum Safety (If Having Issues)[/b][/size]


[list]

[*]Enable Debug: [b]true[/b]
[/list]


This ensures villagers are never throttled at all.


[size=4][b]For Maximum Performance (If Desperate)[/b][/size]


[list]
[*]Update Interval: [b]4-6[/b]
[*]Always Update Villagers: [b]false[/b]
[*]Enable Debug: [b]true[/b]
[/list]


Note: Interval 6+ may cause noticeable NPC behavior delays in background locations.


[size=5][b]Testing Checklist[/b][/size]


After installation, verify:


[list]
[*]Combat in mines feels responsive (monsters move normally)
[*]Eggs/milk production continues normally
[*]Horse riding is smooth
[*]Shop hours are correct
[*]Cutscenes don't freeze
[*]Debug log shows NPC updates being skipped
[/list]


[size=5][b]When This Mod Helps Most[/b][/size]


[b]Use This Mod If:[/b]


[list]
[*]You have 100+ NPCs from expansion mods
[*]You experience stuttering when transitioning between locations
[*]Your CPU is bottlenecking (not GPU)
[*]You spend a lot of time on your farm or in locations with few NPCs while many NPCs exist elsewhere
[/list]


[b]Don't Bother If:[/b]


[list]
[*]You have fewer than 50 total NPCs
[*]Your performance issues are from graphics mods, texture packs, or rendering
[*]Your bottleneck is GPU, not CPU
[/list]


[size=5][b]FAQ[/b][/size]



[size=4][b]Q: Will this break quests?[/b][/size]


[b]A:[/b] Most quests work fine. The mod doesn't affect NPC schedules, just how frequently they update while off-screen. Timed quests with strict meetup requirements should work normally at interval 2-4. If you experience issues with higher intervals, try lowering the setting or enabling "Always Update Villagers."


[size=4][b]Q: Why isn't my FPS improving much?[/b][/size]


[b]A:[/b] NPC update logic is only a small portion of Stardew Valley's total CPU usage. The game spends more time on rendering, player input, physics, audio, UI, and save operations. This mod helps if NPCs are specifically your bottleneck, but won't help with other performance issues.


Additionally, the safety protections mean only background NPCs are throttled. If you spend most of your time in town with 30 NPCs, those 30 are never throttled. Only the NPCs on other maps benefit from throttling.


[size=4][b]Q: Can I use Interval 10 for maximum performance?[/b][/size]


[b]A:[/b] Not recommended. High intervals can cause NPCs to move very slowly in background locations, which may affect quest timing. Interval 2-4 is the safe range. Interval 10 might save an extra 2-3% CPU compared to interval 4, which is unlikely to be noticeable.


[size=4][b]Q: Does this work in multiplayer?[/b][/size]


[b]A:[/b] Untested. Use at your own risk. Each player would need the mod installed.


[size=4][b]Q: My animals aren't producing items![/b][/size]


[b]A:[/b] This should not happen - animals are protected from throttling. Enable debug mode and verify "Animals/Horses (Always)" is counting. If it shows zero, report as a bug.


[size=4][b]Q: Combat feels laggy![/b][/size]


[b]A:[/b] Monsters are protected from throttling. If combat feels laggy, the issue is likely elsewhere. Check your SMAPI log for errors or try disabling other mods.


[size=4][b]Q: How do I know it's working?[/b][/size]


[b]A:[/b] Enable debug logging. You should see statistics every second showing what percentage of NPC update calls are being skipped. With default settings (interval 2), you'll see roughly 40-50% of background NPC updates being skipped.


[size=4][b]Q: What's the difference between the skip percentage and actual performance gain?[/b][/size]


[b]A:[/b] The debug log shows the percentage of NPC update calls being skipped, not the percentage of total game CPU being saved. If NPC updates represent 5% of your total CPU usage, and the mod skips 50% of those calls, you're saving 2.5% of total CPU, not 50%.


[color=#00ffff][size=5][b]Safe Installation & Removal[/b][/size]
[/color]

This mod is [b]100% safe to install and uninstall at any time[/b]. It does not modify your save files in any way.


[list]
[*][b]Installing:[/b] Can be added mid-save with no issues
[*][b]Uninstalling:[/b] Simply remove the mod folder - no save cleanup needed
[*][b]Save files:[/b] Completely unaffected - the mod only changes runtime behavior
[*][b]Switching settings:[/b] All config changes take effect immediately, no save impact
[/list]


The mod uses runtime patches only and never writes to your save file, making it risk-free to test or remove.
